purpose: The fixed map the weekly homework is generated against. Read this BEFORE designing a week. It exists so the pathway is decided once and then followed, instead of being re-derived from scratch every week, which is how the content drifts. This file holds the map only. Where each child currently stands on it is data/curriculum/position.json, which the weekly cycle updates. Do not restate, summarise or re-invent this file in a weekly plan: cite the rung ids.
howToUse: Run scripts/kh.py curriculum <child> to get this map merged with the child's current position, open gaps and the school topic for today. That printout is the brief.
Each section slot 1A to 3C has a fixed purpose that does NOT change week to week. Only the rung inside it moves.
A rung advances only when its advanceWhen condition is met. Not on a hunch, and not because the content feels repetitive.
If a rung has an open gap attached, the next week must re-test that rung. Do not move on.
Anything in hardLimits is absolute. A week that breaks one is wrong even if every other rule passes.
scripts/kh.py validate checks the generated week against this file. Run it before pushing.

mason.target: NSW Selective High School placement test
mason.testShape: Reading, Mathematical Reasoning, Thinking Skills, Writing. Multiple choice under time pressure, plus one writing task.
mason.endState: Reads an unfamiliar non fiction passage once and answers inference questions accurately. Carries out multi step arithmetic including division with remainders without a calculator and checks the result. Solves verbal and numerical reasoning items under about one minute each.
mason.currentPosture: Accuracy is high, around 90 percent. The work now is removing the repeat slips, not adding breadth.

elysia.testShape: Reading, Mathematical Reasoning, Thinking Skills. Multiple choice.
elysia.endState: Reads a short passage and answers literal and simple inference questions. Fluent mental addition and subtraction within 100. Recognises number and shape patterns and explains the rule.
elysia.currentPosture: Accuracy is around 73 percent and the losses are mostly carelessness and incomplete answers rather than missing knowledge. Fluency and finishing the paper matter more than new topics.

1A.format: One passage of 150 to 250 words, then literal and inference questions. At least one question must require joining two facts from different paragraphs.
1A.fixed: Always a passage. Never a standalone question set.
1A.marksNote: Mason's English 20 was re-split on 11 Oct 2026 to make room for writing: 1A 6, 1B 5, 1C 5, 1D 4, from week 25. The subject total is unchanged, so nothing downstream moves.

1B.subject: english
1B.purpose: Sentence level comprehension and grammar in context
1B.format: A short passage or set of sentences, then questions about who, what, when, where, why, how, or about sentence structure.
1B.fixed: Always tied to text the child can point at. Never abstract grammar labelling.

1C.subject: english
1C.purpose: Word level accuracy: spelling, word classes, word building
1C.format: Short items. Use the school spelling list when Nik supplies it.
1C.fixed: Always the week's spelling plus one word knowledge skill.

1D.subject: english
1D.format: One task that names an audience and a text type, as the real paper does: an advice sheet, a letter, a speech, an article, or a narrative. Parent marked against a rubric.
1D.fixed: Always autoMark false with a markScheme. Never a one word answer. The brief always states who is reading it and what kind of text it must be.
1D.why: Writing is 25 percent of the selective mark and had no slot in the week. It sits inside English's 20 rather than inflating the week: 1A 6, 1B 5, 1C 5, 1D 4. Elysia's OC test has no writing paper, so she gets this slot when she turns to the 2031 selective test.

2A.subject: maths
2A.format: A score banded drill. At least 30 problems. First third easy, middle moderate, last third harder. From week 24 Mason's 2A carries 6 of his 20 maths marks rather than 8, with the same 30 items and the bands rescaled.
2A.fixed: Always scoreBand true with scoreBandRules. Always the child's current Kumon arithmetic operation.

2B.subject: maths
2B.purpose: The current Kumon procedure, worked carefully rather than fast
2B.format: 6 or fewer items on one written method, with a worked example box when the last score was under 95 percent.
2B.fixed: Always the single operation the child is currently on in Kumon. Never a mixed bag.

2C.subject: maths
2C.purpose: Applied reasoning on the school's current half term topic
2C.format: Word problems. Mason keeps a couple of remainder or two step problems regardless of the school topic. From week 24 Mason's 2C carries 8 of his 20 maths marks, and 4 of those sit on two 2 mark problems where the answer earns one mark and the written method with its sense check earns the other, marked against a scheme. Nik asked for the working to be worth marks on 11 Oct 2026.
2C.fixed: Always follows schoolSync for today's date. This is the only slot that tracks the school calendar.

3A.subject: thinking
3A.format: A short argument in one or two sentences, then one of: which statement most strengthens it, which most weakens it, which sentence names the mistake made, or which fact would have to be known to test the claim.
3A.fixed: Exactly one defensible answer. The wrong options must be plausible and on topic, not obviously irrelevant.
3A.replaced: Analogies and odd one out on words, re-pointed 11 Oct 2026. Not on the NSW paper.

3B.subject: thinking
3B.format: Sequences and their rules, two unknowns from two totals, a table or chart read for something it does not state, and best value across pack sizes.
3B.fixed: Number sets must mix odd and even inside the rule so the odd or even shortcut fails, and no number may be the only odd or the only even one in the set. Every data item must be answerable from the table alone.

3C.subject: thinking
3C.format: Conditional statements and what follows from them, two speakers of whom one reasons correctly, constraint puzzles from three or more clues, the minimum needed to guarantee an outcome, and counting events over a date range.
3C.fixed: Every item must be solvable from the information given. No outside knowledge. Exactly one consistent solution.
3C.replaced: Caesar ciphers and substitution codes, re-pointed 11 Oct 2026. Not on the NSW paper.

elysia.rule: Multiplication and division facts may only use the 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10 times tables. Never the 7, 8, 9, 11 or 12 tables.
elysia.why: She practises those six daily at home. School only teaches 2, 5 and 10 from January 2027.

elysia.rule: No written (column or long) multiplication or division.
Time to the minute is allowed: Nik confirmed on 4 Oct 2026 that she is already learning it at home. Keep the two times inside the same hour for now, and do not assume the school has taught it.
elysia.why: Ahead of the school sequence, which reaches it in Summer 2 2027, but practised at home.

mason.rule: No question may require a calculator.
mason.why: The selective test is non calculator.

mason.rule: Thinking Skills items must be solvable from the information given. No general knowledge.

Every Thinking Skills item must be one of the NSW families: strengthen, weaken, name the flaw, what evidence would settle it, conditional reasoning, whose reasoning is correct, constraint puzzle, data deduction, best value, calendar count. No analogies, no letter codes, no ciphers.
mason.why: Counted across the Department's own practice paper. Analogies and ciphers appear nowhere on it.

mason.rule: Slot 1D must name the audience and the text type, and must be autoMark false with a markScheme.
mason.why: The real task is of the form write an advice sheet for three new students, not write a story.

both.rule: Odd one out and analogy items must have exactly one defensible answer. No two valid splits.
Number sets must mix odd and even inside the rule so the odd or even shortcut fails, and no number may be the only odd or the only even one in the set. At least two of each.
If a test is meant to be unhinted, the passage must not print the answer rule.
both.why: A hinted pass cannot resolve a gap. It records true but stays IMPROVING.

both.rule: No more than 2 identical answers in any set of short answers.
No em dashes in child facing text.
Every sum, key and cipher is computed by script, never written by hand.
